messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
version:3.1.0
IP:192.168.11.33
API name: get nodes list
Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of nodes associated with a specified fabric in a network. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to. The URL should include the target IP, API endpoint, and the fabricName query parameter placeholder https://<ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric whose nodes are to be listed. This value is used to replace the {fabricName} placeholder in the URL.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?" They provide version, IP, API name, and parameter. They want to generate a RESTful API request. We have a tool function to send HTTP GET request. We can use that. The function expects url and fabricName. The default URL includes placeholder. We need to replace placeholder with fabricName. So we call functions.requests_get with url: "https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI" and fabricName: "PEK-ACI". Then we can output the result. The user likely wants to see how to generate the request. We can show the URL and then call the function. We'll do that.
